questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

International Mother Earth Day is celebrated (1)/ every year to remind us that the Earth provides us with life (2)/ and we should be grudgeful for the same. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in the third part of the given sentence as one should be ‘grateful’ or thankful to the Earth for all it provides. ‘Grudgeful’ refers to someone who holds bitterness against someone. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

A shepherd boy (1)/ tended his masters sheep (2)/ near a dark forest not far from the village. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: ‘To tend’ means to look after. The given sentence carries the meaning that the shepherd boy looked after the sheep that *belonged to the master*. Thus the possessive form of master/ masters should be used, i.e., master’s or masters' (if there are more than one masters).

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Her heart was ______ with joy.
questions.solution: ‘Was’ indicates that the action happened in the past, therefore the past form of the word ‘fill’ should be used. Thus option 3 is the correct answer. ‘Fulled’ is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Abhishek has a bad habit of ______ his car keys.
questions.solution:
Among all the given options, ‘misplacing’ conveys the correct meaning. Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

From the sentence, it is evident that a participle would fit the blank. The present participle form of the base form of the verb 'misplace' is 'misplacing'

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

His father won't be able to leave for Mumbai (until they have arrived).
questions.solution: The first clause of the given sentence talks about an action that will take place in the future. The clause after ‘until’ indicates the condition for it. In a sentence where the main clause is in the future, the subordinate sentence introduced by a time conjunction (when, while, by the time, until, etc.) must remain in the present tense. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

One who hoards wealth and spends as little money as possible
questions.solution:
*One who hoards wealth and spends as little money as possible* is known as a miser. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

The other options are not synonymous with miser:

 
• Member means a person who belongs to a group or organization.
 
• Macho means behaving or appearing to behave in a way that is stereotypically masculine.
 
• Militant means supporting or engaging in extreme or unyielding methods of achieving political or social goals.

questions.question: A and B starts from same point and walks 30 km in opposite directions to each other. A turns left and walks 10 km. B turns left and walks 10 km. How far (in km) are they from each other?
questions.solution:
Based on given information direction diagram can be traced as,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43d749c9d5f02762d5879975c8b3af880dda8fa623a3a07e25912e43fbb2170d.png] 

Distance between A and B = AB = OA + OB

OA = √(30)² + (10)² = √(900 + 100) = √1000 = 10 √10 km

Similarly,

OB = OA = √(30)² + (10)² = √(900 + 100) = √1000 = 10 √10 km

Therefore, A and B are 20√10 km (10√10 + 10√10) far away from each other.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "EURO" is written as "DTQN". How is "FAKE" written in that code language?
In a certain code language, "BUS" is written as "43" and "BUY" is written as "49". How is "CAP" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
With reference to English alphabet,

B = 2, U = 21, S = 19

⇒ BUS + 1 = B + U + S + 1 = 2 + 21 + 19 + 1 = 43

Similarly,

B = 2, U = 21, Y = 25

⇒ BUY = B + U + Y + 1 = 2 + 21 + 25 + 1 = 49

Similarly,

C = 3, A = 1, P = 16

⇒ CAP + 1 = C + A + P + 1 = 3 + 1 + 16 + 1 = 21

Hence, in the given code language “CAP” written as “21”.

questions.question: How many numbers are there from 500 to 590 which are divisible by both 2 and 7?
questions.solution:
If a number is divisible by both 2 and 7, then the number should be divisible by their LCM.

LCM of 2 and 7 = 2 × 7 = 14

Now,

14 × 36 = 504

14 × 37 = 518

14 × 38 = 532

14 × 39 = 546

14 × 40 = 560

14 × 41 = 574

14 × 42 = 588

∴ 7 numbers are there from 500 to 590 which are divisible by both 2 and 7.

P alone can do a work in 25 days. P is 40% less efficient than Q. In how many days can Q alone do the work?
questions.solution:
P alone can do a work in 25 days

Part of work done by P in a day = 1/25

P is 40% less efficient than Q

∴ Part of work done by P in a day = (1 - 0.40) × Part of work done by Q in a day

⇒ 1/25 = 0.60 × Part of work done by Q in a day

⇒ Part of work done by Q in a day = 1/(25 × 0.60)

⇒ Part of work done by Q in a day = 1/15

∴ Q can complete the work in 15 days

questions.question: A wholesaler offers 10% discount on pens which have been marked 60% above the cost price. Sumit bought the pen for Rs 504. What was the cost price (in Rs) of the pens?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

Cost price = 504 × (100/160) × (100/90) = Rs. 350

**Detailed Solution:**

Let the cost price of pens be Rs. x

Marked price is 60% above the cost price

∴ Marked price = Rs. 1.60x

Discount = 10%

∴ Selling price = Rs. (0.90 × 1.60x) = Rs. 1.44x

Sumit bought the pen for Rs. 504, it means the Wholesaler sold the pen for Rs. 504

Selling price = Rs. 504

∴ 1.44x = Rs. 504

⇒ x = Rs. 350

⇒ 11m = 140 × 66

⇒ m = 140 × 6

⇒ m = 840

= 4 × 1020

questions.question: By selling 40 grams of rice, a person loss the cost price of 20 grams of rice. Find his loss percent?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of 1 gram = Rs. x

∴ Cost price of 40 gram = Rs. 40x

Cost price of 20 gram = Rs. 20x

By selling 40 grams of rice, a person loss the cost price of 20 grams

∴ Loss percentage = frac{{Loss}}{{Cost price}} times 100

 = frac{{20x}}{{40x}} times 100

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 50 km/hr. It covers a distance of 500 km upstream in 20 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the stream?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the stream = x km/hr

Given,

Speed of the boat in still water = 50 km/hr

∴ Speed of the boat towards upstream = (50 - x) km/hr

Distance covered = 500 km

Time taken = 20 hr

∵ Distance covered = Speed × Time taken

⇒ 500 = (50 - x) × 20

⇒ 25 = (50 - x)

⇒ x = 25 km/hr

⇒ Time = 144 sec

questions.question: ______ covers those enterprises or places of work where the terms of employment are regular.
questions.solution:
• Organised sector is the sector where the terms of employment are fixed and the employees have the assured work.
 
• There are number of acts which apply to the organised sector like, *Bonus Act, Factories Act, Minimum Wages Act, PF Act,* etc.
 
• The rules of the government are strictly followed in the organisational sector.
 
• The salaries of the employees in the organised sector are as per the government norms.

questions.question: What can be said about the interest rate on loans when compared to the interest rate offered on deposits?

options.text: It may be higher or lower

questions.solution:
• Interest rate on loans is **always higher** than the interest rate offered on deposits.
 
• Bank makes profit by charging higher interest rate on loans than the interest they pay on the accounts of depositors.
 
• Interest rate on loan is the percentage of the principal which is charged by the lender for the use of its money.
 
• Bank charges fixed or variable interest rates.

questions.question: Who is the supreme law-making institution in India?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Parliament of India** is the supreme law-making institution in India.
 
• **Parliament** is composed of the **President** of Indian and the two houses which are **Rajya Sabha** and **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The proposal of legislatives is brought before house of Parliament in the form of the bill.
 
• The bill becomes an Act of Parliament when the draft of the legislative proposal is passed by both houses of Parliament and assented to by the President.
 
• The council of the states have power to make the recommendations over the bills to the house within a period of 14 days.

questions.question: When did Constituent Assembly adopt Constitution?
questions.solution:
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the **Constituent Assembly** on **26th November, 1949** but it **came into force on 26th January, 1950**.
 
• **Constitution of India** is known as the **supreme law of India** which consists of fundamental political codes, powers, procedures, structures and the duties of the government institutions, directive principles and the duties of the citizen.
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• **B.R. Ambedkar** was considered to be its chief architect as he was the **Chairman** of the **Drafting** **Committee**.

questions.question: In which year Swadeshi Movement started?

questions.question: The experiment which led to the discovery of nucleus was performed by ______.
questions.solution:

• Wetlands consist of more vascular plants that have been adapted to saturated soil.
 
• For agriculture related purposes, Wetlands are converted into dry land with dikes and drains.

questions.question: Which is NOT among the 3 rivers of Indus water system over which Pakistan got control under Indus Water Treaty with India?
questions.solution:
• The control over **Ravi **was not given to Pakistan as per the treaty.
 
• **Indus Water Treaty** was signed on **9th September, 1960** in **Karachi.**
 
• The Treaty administers the utilisation of water of river Indus and its tributaries by both the countries.
 
• According to treaty, rivers **Beas, Ravi** and **Sutlej** are under the jurisdiction of **India** while **Indus**, **Chenab** and **Jhelum** are under the jurisdiction of **Pakistan**.
 
• Permanent Indus Commission was set up as bilateral commission to implement and manage the treaty.
